subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed allowed-plus-blocked result sets can proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or keep the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed rule?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but it changes the default outbound-fetch security boundary and must reflect maintainer intent rather than an automated policy guess.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into pinned connection paths, and keep all-blocked result sets rejected.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat the current strict behavior as intentional and direct affected operators to trusted proxy or explicit fake-IP policy configuration where applicable.

options.title: Make mixed DNS tolerance explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an operator-controlled policy for DNS-polluted environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into pinned connection paths, and keep all-blocked result sets rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: The central SSRF policy history most directly points to this owner for the security-boundary decision.
